title: Queued-output throttling and stale-generation sweeper
creator: Priya Patel
description: Introduce a server-side queued-output throttling mechanism and a background sweeper for stale/incomplete generations to reduce memory pressure and avoid unbounded growth of partial outputs when clients disconnect or timeout.
background: We continue seeing memory/external store usage spikes from long-lived partial generations that never complete (clients disconnect mid-stream, legacy SDKs that don't resume, mobile apps killed). Existing heuristics are ad-hoc TTLs; we need a deterministic reclaim approach with low false-positive reclamation risk and clear observability for customers.
goals: 1) Provide graceful per-client backpressure that slows producers without dropping in-progress work. 2) Reclaim stale partial outputs reliably with low impact to resumed clients. 3) Preserve atomicity for tool/function-call outputs so tool side-effects are not lost. 4) Offer clear metrics and dashboarding for operations and customers.
non_goals: Replacing end-to-end client retry/resume semantics or forcing changes in client SDKs. This ticket implements server-side controls and a compatibility shim for older clients; full client SDK rollout is a separate workstream.
proposal_summary: Implement a two-part solution: (A) queued-output throttling: per-connection output queue limits + adaptive pause frames and a soft-circuit-breaker that tells producers to slow generation; (B) stale-generation sweeper: a background reclaim process that marks, checkpoints, and then deletes partial artifacts after an adaptive grace window. Add resume-token mapping and a compatibility shim to reduce resume failures for legacy clients.
api_changes: Add optional response and request headers: 'X-Redwood-Resume-Token' (response) for new resume flow, 'X-Partial-Mode' (request) with values ['eager','durable','ephemeral'] to indicate customer preference for retention. Streaming protocol introduces PAUSE/RESUME control frames for clients that support the new streaming protocol. Legacy clients continue receiving existing chunked responses.
server_side_design:
- Per-connection queued output (bounded ring buffer): default 128KB per active request. When full, runtime emits a PAUSE frame to the model proxy and begins backpressure signaling.
- Soft-circuit-breaker: if queue pressure persists > configurable threshold (2000ms), raise generation priority-lowering policy and optionally truncate the oldest buffered deltas to keep latency SLOs.
- Ephemeral vs Durable partials: ephemeral partials live in memory/fast cache and expire quickly; durable partials are checkpointed to object store and are reclaimable by sweeper.
- Resume-token mapping: server generates a short-lived resume token (UUID) mapped to checkpoint metadata in KV store with TTL; clients can supply the token to resume. For legacy clients we create a one-shot mapped token when we detect a disconnect and return a 202-wait style header so they can poll.
reclamation_algorithm: 1) Mark phase: sweeper scans checkpoint index for partials with last_activity < adaptive_TTL. adaptive_TTL = base_TTL * (1 + avg_seq_len/seq_norm) where avg_seq_len is per-customer running average. 2) Grace checkpoint: set state='marked' and emit audit event; notify any linked customer webhooks. 3) Soft reclaim window (2 minutes): if client resumes, unmark and allow resume; otherwise delete artifacts into 'reclaimed' bucket and increment reclaimed_count metric. 4) Probabilistic early compaction: when disk pressure high, compact partials by removing expensive blobs but keep metadata for potential resume with degraded fidelity.
function_call_handling: Function/tool-call outputs are pinned: any partial generation that contains an inbound function call or outgoing tool invocation is exempt from automatic deletion until the invocation result is committed or fails with a terminal state. The sweeper consults invocation state in the tool-run index before deleting. This prevents losing side-effects or orphaned external operations.
edge_cases: - Mobile OS kills: fallback tokens are provided but TTLs are short. - Legacy SDKs without resume support: server returns a 'resume_hint' header and creates a one-time durable snapshot (costly) for a short window. - Cross-region resume: resume token contains region affinity; server routes resume requests to original region where possible, else proxies state.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): feature-flag queued-output throttling in runtime-1.23 for 5% of traffic (internal + pilot customers) with soft defaults. Phase 2 (observability): add dashboards and alerts. Phase 3 (wider rollout): enable sweeper for non-critical customers and tune TTLs. Phase 4 (GA): enable default for all hosted tenants and document header-based opt-in for private deployments.
dashboards: Create a per-tenant dashboard showing queued_bytes, pause_frames, resume success rate, reclaimed artifacts, and cost saved via reclaimed artifacts. Add an alert if queued_bytes_per_conn > 4x baseline for 5m.
qa_tests: - Simulate abrupt client disconnect mid-stream and validate PAUSE/RESUME behavior and token issuance. - Verify sweeper respects pinned function-call partials. - Load test with many small partials to validate reclamation does not impact latency SLO. - Back-compat tests for legacy SDKs: ensure resume_hint header triggers one-shot snapshot creation and successful recovery for at least 60s.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false-positive reclamation causing user-visible lost generations. Mitigation: two-step mark+grace process, webhook notifications, and conservative default TTLs. Risk: increased object-store cost due to one-shot durable snapshots for legacy clients. Mitigation: limit legacy snapshot window and expose cost label for tenant opt-in.
docs_needed: SDK changelog entry describing headers and resume flow, runtime docs for feature flags and configuration knobs, and a KB article on tuning TTLs for latency-sensitive workloads.
implementation_steps: Add queued-output ring buffer and PAUSE/RESUME frames in runtime proxy
Implement soft-circuit-breaker and priority-lowering policy module
Resume-token KV index and one-shot snapshot creation for legacy clients
Sweeper service: mark->grace->reclaim workflow with audit events
Wire up metrics and build dashboards/alerts
blockers: infra-ticket for extra ephemeral cache capacity
